summary_html: The **Project Milk Carton AI Layer** performs cross-analysis of federal and state chains to identify weak points, policy gaps, and non-compliance. This is the citizen feedback mechanism for accountability and reform.
authority_html: No direct statutory authority — citizen innovation layer built on public data and federal transparency laws.

primary_citations.citation_text: District of Columbia - D.C. Code Title 4, Chapter 13 (Child Abuse and Neglect)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States District Court for the District of Columbia
key_cases.holding: After trial the court found the District's child welfare system violated federal and District statutory and constitutional requirements at nearly every stage, including a consistent failure to provide services or make reasonable efforts to prevent placement, and ordered systemic relief.
key_cases.relevance: It is the foundational systemic-failure dataset for any cross-layer analysis of the District's chain.
key_cases.quote: the Court finds that defendants have consistently failed to provide services or otherwise use “reasonable efforts” to prevent placement

key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: Sitting en banc the court overruled In re K.M.T. and held that an order changing a neglected child's permanency goal from reunification to adoption is an immediately appealable final order, that permanency goal review hearings must protect parental due process, that the court must first find by a preponderance that the government made reasonable efforts toward reunification, and that a finding of parental unfitness must precede termination absent truly exceptional circumstances or stipulation.
key_cases.relevance: It is the single most important structural holding a cross-jurisdiction analysis of D.C. permanency decision-making must account for.
key_cases.quote: a change of the presumptive goal of a neglect proceeding from reunification to adoption is an appealable final order

key_cases.case_name: Vining v. Council of the District of Columbia
key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: The Council may not invoke the Legislative Privilege Act through D.C. FOIA Exemption 6 (or, on this record, Exemption 4) to withhold documents responsive to a FOIA request, and summary judgment for the Council was reversed.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes that the District record base a public analysis depends on is presumptively disclosable.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the Legislative Privilege Act cannot be invoked through Exemption 6 so as to permit the Council to withhold documents responsive to a FOIA request

key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: The court dismissed the mother's appeals for lack of jurisdiction, holding that an order changing a permanency planning goal is only a step toward final disposition, does not affect the parents' substantive rights, and therefore is not a final appealable order.
key_cases.relevance: It governs the District's pre-2016 permanency record, in which goal changes from reunification to adoption were made with no possibility of appellate correction at all.
key_cases.quote: We hold accordingly that an order changing a permanency planning goal is not final or appealable.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
key_cases.holding: Sitting en banc the court held there is no 'jurisdictional question' exception to the law-of-the-case doctrine, so the later panel could not revisit the earlier panel's direction that the district court exercise pendent jurisdiction over the local-law claims in the foster care class action, and it remitted the District's remaining arguments to the panel.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes what the en banc court actually decided — law of the case and pendent jurisdiction, not the merits — so a cross-layer analysis does not overstate appellate endorsement of the District's systemic-failure findings.
key_cases.quote: the law-of-the-case and law-of-the-circuit doctrines precluded the panel in LaShawn II from revisiting the Gibbs step two decision reached in LaShawn I

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately if MPD deems the child critical missing; otherwise once the child has been missing more than 30 days (MPD makes the NCMEC report)
timeline_requirements.starts_from: CFSA files a missing person report with MPD immediately after discovering the child is missing (D.C. Code § 4-1323.01(a))
